summary: All 14 lessons carried exam-form errors: 60 of 84 practice questions were in forms this paper never sets (8-mark 'Explain why', 'Explain the importance', 'Describe two features' on the thematic study, an analytical narrative, a 12-mark historic environment essay, 16-mark judgements on Whitechapel and single-source utility questions), and every exam tip named a wrong tariff. Three source questions rested on fabricated documents with invented archive provenances. Twenty-six invented examiner or mark-band claims were removed. Sixteen factual errors were corrected, the heaviest being the Pitchfork DNA conviction (1988, not 1986), the Race Relations Act 1965 attributed to Roy Jenkins, Elizabeth Fry meeting Queen Victoria in the 1820s, Eddowes photographed in Mitre Square, Lord Melbourne as Prime Minister in 1832, and a two-thirds transportation figure for 1700.
